chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Isma'il told me, saying: Al-Nu'man ibn Abi al-Dalhas al-Baladi narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Layla, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The truly sincere (al-Siddiqun) are three: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Habib al-Najjar, and the believer from the family of Pharaoh.

key_terms.الصِّدِّيقُونَ: The truly sincere ones; a title for those with the highest degree of truthfulness in faith and action.
key_terms.حَبِيبُ النَّجَّارِ: Habib the Carpenter, a companion of Prophet Jesus (Isa) mentioned in the Quran.
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: Ali ibn Abi Talib, the cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad.
key_terms.مُؤْمِنُ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ: The Believer from the Family of Pharaoh, a righteous man from Pharaoh's clan who supported Moses.

ai.seo_question: Who are the three truly sincere believers (al-Siddiqun) mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three figures as the archetypes of 'al-Siddiqun' (the most truthful), linking the highest tier of prophetic companionship (Ali) with the righteous outsiders of the Quranic narrative (Habib al-Najjar and the Pharaoh's believer). This classification underscores the universality of true sincerity, transcending lineage or social status, and is often cited in Shia theology to validate Ali's preeminent status alongside other exemplary believers.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-254 Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Isma’il narrated that Al-Nue’man ibn Abil Dalhas al-Baladi quoted Al-Hussein ibn Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Musa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Layli that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,
“The truly sincere believers are three: Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB), Habib - the carpenter , and the believer from the family of Pharaoh (Hizkil ).”
